Battle of the Camel: Iraq. The Battle of the Camel, also known as the Battle of Basra (Arabic: معركة الجمل, romanized: Maʿrakat al-Jamal) took place in 656 CE outside of Basra in Iraq.

Novgorod Republic: Old East Slavic. For much of its history, Novgorod was the center of Russian art and culture.

The son of a Trojan prince and the goddess Aphrodite, this mythological hero appears only briefly in Homer's Iliad but receives an entire Roman epic devoted to his journey — who is he?
Aeneas (in-; Classical; from Ancient) was a Trojan hero in Greco-Roman mythology, the son of the Trojan prince Anchises and the Greek goddess Aphrodite (equivalent to the Roman Venus).
She has led the AfD's parliamentary group in the Bundestag since 2017 and now co-chairs the party with Tino Chrupalla — which German politician is it?

Alice Weidel (born 6 February 1979) is a German far-right politician who has been serving as co-chairwoman of the far-right, vlkisch nationalist Alternative for Germany (AfD) party alongside Tino Chrupalla since June 2022.
A career diplomat who advocated for the 2003 invasion of Iraq, this man went on to serve as the 71st U.S. secretary of state from 2021 to 2025 — who is he?
Antony Blinken (born April 16, 1962) is an American lawyer and diplomat who served as the 71st United States secretary of state from 2021 to 2025.

Originally depicted as a lioness, this ancient Egyptian goddess was later associated with the domestic cat and worshipped as early as 2890 BCE, sharing a dual nature with the warrior goddess Sekhmet — who is she?
Bastet (Ancient), also known as Ubasti or Bubastis, is a goddess of ancient Egyptian religion, possibly of Nubian origin, worshipped as early as the Second Dynasty (2890 BCE).
Believed to have once been an NKVD informant, this Polish communist led his country from 1948 to 1956 and imposed the Stalinist system there — who was he?
Bolesław Bierut (18 April 1892 - 12 March 1956) was a Polish communist activist and politician who was the leader of communist-ruled Poland from 1948 until 1956.

Eton-educated and aristocratic, this British general is best remembered for his 1781 surrender at Yorktown — yet he later governed both Ireland and India, where his name lives on in a famous legal code. Who was he?
Charles Cornwallis, 1st Marquess Cornwallis (31 December 1738 - 5 October 1805) was a British Army officer, Whig politician and colonial administrator.
This immensely wealthy final king of Lydia fell to Cyrus the Great after the fall of his capital, Sardis, in the 6th century BC — who was he?
Croesus (Ancient) was the last king of Lydia from 585 BC to 546 BC.
After a term as Russia's president, he swapped chairs to become prime minister from 2012 to 2020, and now serves as deputy chairman of the Security Council — which Russian politician is this?
Dmitry Medvedev (born 14 September 1965) is a Russian politician and lawyer who served as the president of Russia from 2008 to 2012 and as the prime minister of Russia from 2012 to 2020.
Dubbed the 'Father of the Nation' and also a noted historian behind the book Capitalism and Slavery, this leader steered Trinidad and Tobago to independence — who is it?
Eric Williams (25 September 1911 - 29 March 1981) was a Trinidad and Tobago politician.

This Dutch politician served as First Vice-President of the European Commission under Jean-Claude Juncker, later became the EU's climate action commissioner, and then led a Dutch political alliance in parliament from 2023 to 2025. Who is he?
Frans Timmermans (born 6 May 1961) is a Dutch politician who was the leader of GroenLinks-PvdA in the House of Representatives from 2023 to 2025.
Working alongside Simone de Beauvoir to expose torture during the Algerian War, this feminist lawyer later signed a landmark 1971 declaration demanding free abortion access — who is she?
Gisèle Halimi (born Zeiza Gisle lise Taeb,; 27 July 1927 - 28 July 2020) was a Tunisian-French lawyer, politician, essayist and feminist activist.
As China's top leader on Hong Kong and Macau affairs, this former Shanghai mayor rose to the Politburo Standing Committee before becoming vice president in 2023 — who is he?
Han Zheng (pinyin: Hn Zhng; born April 1955) is a Chinese politician who, since 2023, has served as the 11th vice president of China.
Dated to begin about 5,200 years ago with the invention of writing, this scholarly record traces humanity's religious feelings, thoughts, and ideas across the millennia — what field of study is this?
History of religion is the written record of human religious feelings, thoughts, and ideas.
A professor of Ukrainian language and a nationalist member of parliament from 2012 to 2014, this linguist campaigned hard for heritage-language learning - who is she?
Iryna Farion (29 April 1964 - 19 July 2024) was a Ukrainian linguist and nationalist politician who served as a deputy in the Verkhovna Rada from 2012 to 2014.

Elected New York's first female county judge and later county district attorney, this Lebanese-American TV host and lawyer has served as the U.S. attorney for the District of Columbia since May 2025. Who is she?
Jeanine Pirro (born June 2, 1951) is a Lebanese-American television host, lawyer, and author who has been serving as the United States attorney for the District of Columbia since May 2025.
This Nova Scotian-born seaman turned his record-setting solo voyage aboard the Spray into the best-seller "Sailing Alone Around the World" — who was he?
Joshua Slocum (February 20, 1844 - on or shortly after November 14, 1909) was the first person to sail single-handedly around the world.
Commander of the Tobruk-based Libyan National Army, this officer has been the de facto ruler of eastern Libya since 2017, governing it as a military dictatorship. Who is he?
Khalifa Haftar (born 7 November 1943) is a Libyan politician, military officer, and the commander of the Tobruk-based Libyan National Army (LNA).
Born Lev Bronstein, this Marxist theorist stood with Lenin as one of the two most prominent figures of the early Soviet state — until he was exiled in 1929 and assassinated in 1940. Who was he?
Leon Trotsky was Soviet politician and revolutionary (1879–1940).
Chancellor of a university in Haryana and MLA for Tijara in Rajasthan, this politician also serves as the eighth head of a Hindu monastic sect — who is he?
Mahant Balaknath (born 16 April 1984) is an Indian politician and current MLA from Tijara constituency in Rajasthan.
This French politician has led the La France Insoumise parliamentary group in the National Assembly since 2021, having represented a Val-de-Marne constituency since 2017 — who is she?
Mathilde Panot (French; born 15 January 1989) is a French politician who has served as the president of the La France Insoumise group in the National Assembly since October 2021.
This Roman goddess of wisdom and strategic warfare shared the Capitoline Triad with Jupiter and Juno, and is often shown with an owl — who is she?
Minerva is the Roman goddess of wisdom, justice, law, victory, and the sponsor of arts, trade, and strategy.
While 'nudism' stresses the practice itself, this near-synonym highlights an attitude of harmony with nature woven into non-sexual social nudity — which term?
Naturism is a lifestyle of practicing non-sexual social nudity in private and in public; the word also refers to the cultural movement which advocates and defends that lifestyle.
Marked by financial and personal failure before 1640, this English soldier rose to lead Parliament's army, championed the execution of Charles I, and ruled as Lord Protector. Who is he?
Oliver Cromwell (25 April 1599 - 3 September 1658) was an English statesman, farmer and soldier, widely regarded as one of the most important figures in British history.
This historical region in southwestern Iran, corresponding to Fars province, saw Iranic-speaking migrants arrive from Central Asia in ancient times — what is it called?
Persis is a historical region in south-western Iran, roughly corresponding with Fars province.

Officially known as the Religious Society of Friends, members of this Christian movement got their popular nickname after founder George Fox told a judge to 'quake before the authority of God' — what are they called?
Quakers are people who belong to the Religious Society of Friends, originally known as simply the Society of Friends, a historically Protestant Christian set of denominations.
A decorated Vietnam Marine awarded a Bronze Star and Purple Heart, he led the FBI as its sixth director from 2001 to 2013 after appointments under presidents of both parties. Who?
Robert Mueller (August 7, 1944 - March 20, 2026) was an American lawyer who served as the sixth director of the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) from 2001 to 2013.

Widely expected to succeed his mother as India's prime minister, this politician's sudden death in a 1980 plane crash instead paved the way for his older brother to inherit that political legacy — who was he?
Sanjay Gandhi (14 December 1946 - 23 June 1980) was an Indian politician.

This Yugoslav and Serbian politician served as president of Serbia (1989–1997) and then the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia (1997–2000). He was the first sitting head of state charged with war crimes. Who is he?

Slobodan Milošević (Serbian) was a Yugoslav and Serbian politician who was the president of Serbia between 1989 and 1997 and president of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia from 1997 until his overthrow in 2000.
With an unclassified script of just 97 known inscriptions, this Bronze Age Iberian culture is considered the first named kingdom of southwestern Spain — which civilization?
Tartessos is, as defined by archaeological discoveries, a historical civilization settled in the southern Iberian Peninsula from about the late Bronze Age until the 5th century BC.

Led by Gamal Abdel Nasser, this short-lived political union between Egypt and Syria existed from 1958 until Syria seceded following a 1961 coup, with Egypt keeping the joint name until 1971 — what was this country called?
United Arab Republic was a country and sovereign state in the Middle East from 1958 to 1971.
After forcing the last Qing emperor's abdication and later dying in 1916, Yuan Shikai left behind a power vacuum that split China among competing military strongmen — which turbulent period followed?

Warlord Era was the period in the history of the Republic of China between 1916 and 1928, when control of the country was divided between rival military cliques of the Beiyang Army and other regional factions.

A longtime Communist Party member and labour lawyer, this Spanish politician founded an electoral alliance in 2023 while serving as her country's Minister of Labour and Second Deputy Prime Minister — who is she?

Yolanda Díaz (born 6 May 1971) is a Spanish politician and labour lawyer, currently serving as Second Deputy Prime Minister since 2021, and Minister of Labour and Social Economy of the Government of Spain since 2020.

Abdullah Gül: President of Turkey from 2007 to 2014. Abdullah Gül (born 29 October 1950) is a Turkish politician who served as the president of Turkey from 2007 to 2014.

Alfred Deakin: Prime Minister of Australia (1903–1904; 1905–1908; 1909–1910)

Born on Delos as the twin sister of Apollo, this Greek goddess presided over hunting, wild animals, and childbirth while herself remaining chaste — who is she?
Artemis: Ancient Greek goddess. In one account, Artemis is born first and then proceeds to assist Leto in the birth of the second twin, Apollo.

Benito Juárez: President of Mexico from 1858 to 1872.

Boris Yeltsin: President of Russia from 1991 to 1999. Boris Nikolayevich Yeltsin (1 February 1931 – 23 April 2007) was a Soviet and Russian politician who served as President of Russia from 1991 to 1999.
This Warsaw-born nobleman fought against foreign domination of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth before crossing the Atlantic to earn the title "The Father of American cavalry" — who was he?
Casimir Pulaski: Polish nobleman and American Revolutionary War general (1745–1779)
This Republican served as the 55th governor of New Jersey and later ran for his party's presidential nomination in both 2016 and 2024 — who is he?
Chris Christie: Governor of New Jersey from 2010 to 2018.

Emerging in Western Europe and the US during the Industrial Revolution, this socio-cultural phenomenon turns the acquisition of goods into something that shapes identity, not just meets basic needs — which term?
Consumerism: Acquisition of goods beyond essential needs.

David I of Scotland: King of Alba from 1124 to 1153.

Edward the Elder: King of the Anglo-Saxons from 899 to 924.

Erick Thohir: Indonesian politician and businessman (born 1970)

Free will: Ability to make choices voluntarily.

George VI: King of the United Kingdom from 1936 to 1952.
Serving as Texas's attorney general before becoming its governor in 2015, this Republican is now the longest-serving incumbent governor in the United States — who is he?

Greg Abbott: Governor of Texas since 2015. Gregory Wayne Abbott ( ABB-ət; born November 13, 1957) is an American politician, attorney, and jurist who has served since 2015 as the 48th governor of Texas.
Growing out of Lübeck in the late 12th century, which medieval trading network eventually spanned nearly 200 towns from Estonia to the Netherlands?
Hanseatic League: 1200s–1669 trade confederation in Northern Europe.

Hephthalites: 5th–8th-century nomadic confederation in Central Asia.
Adopted in 1917 to shed a German-sounding surname amid wartime sentiment, this royal lineage has included five monarchs, from George V to Charles III — which royal family?
House of Windsor: British royal family. The House of Windsor is the current royal house of the United Kingdom and other Commonwealth realms.
Known to the Akkadians as Ishtar and symbolized by a lion and an eight-pointed star, which Mesopotamian goddess of war and love was worshipped at a temple in Uruk?
Inanna: Ancient Mesopotamian goddess. Inanna was worshipped in Sumer as early as the Uruk period (c. 4000 – 3100 BCE), and her worship was relatively localized before the conquest of Sargon of Akkad.
A last-minute swap onto the Apollo 13 crew, this command module pilot rode the famous aborted mission farther from Earth than any astronaut would travel for decades — who was he?
Jack Swigert: American astronaut and politician (1931–1982)

Sister of a president, two U.S. senators, and the founder of the Special Olympics, this diplomat served as U.S. Ambassador to Ireland and convinced Bill Clinton to grant a controversial visa to a Sinn Féin leader — who is she?

Jules Dumont d'Urville: French explorer and naval officer (1790–1842)
Nicknamed "The Conqueror," this King of Dál Riada subdued the Picts in the 840s and moved the Stone of Scone to his new capital at Forteviot — who was he?
Kenneth MacAlpin: King of the Picts from 848 to 858.
Ruling the Vijayanagara Empire at its political and cultural peak from 1509 to 1529, this emperor defeated the sultans of Bijapur and Golconda and conquered the Raichur Doab in 1512 — who was he?

Krishnadevaraya: Emperor of Vijayanagara from 1509 to 1529. Krishnadevaraya (17 January 1471 – 17 October 1529) was emperor of the Vijayanagara Empire from 1509 to 1529 and the third ruler of the Tuluva dynasty.
This Argentine general seized the presidency by ousting his predecessor in 1981, backed the Contras in Nicaragua, and continued the military junta's 'Dirty War' — who is he?
Leopoldo Galtieri: Argentine general and military ruler (1926–2003)
Legend credits this man with toppling Rome's last king after the suicide of Lucretia and becoming one of the Republic's first two consuls — who was he?
Lucius Junius Brutus: Semi-legendary 6th-century BC founder of Roman Republic.

Mallikarjun Kharge: Indian lawyer and politician (born 1942)
Elected to the Chamber of Deputies in the 2018 Italian general election, this politician represents the Forza Italia party — who is she?

Named after a 16th-century Frisian cleric, this Anabaptist Christian movement traces to the Radical Reformation and later codified beliefs like adult baptism and foot washing in its 1632 Dordrecht Confession — what is it called?
Mennonites: Anabaptist groups originating in Western Europe.
Ruler of the Kingdom of Pontus in northern Anatolia, this king waged repeated but unsuccessful wars against Rome for dominance over Asia Minor and the Black Sea — who was he?
Mithridates VI Eupator: King of Pontus from 120 to 63 BC.
During this Ottoman sultan's reign Morocco briefly became a vassal before breaking free, and ties with Elizabethan England were forged over a shared enemy; who was this 16th-century ruler?
Murad III: Sultan of the Ottoman Empire from 1574 to 1595.
Born into a prominent Catholic mandarin family, he became South Vietnam's first president in 1955 and ruled until his assassination during a CIA-backed coup in 1963 — who was he?

Ngo Dinh Diem: President of South Vietnam from 1955 to 1963. Diệm was born into a prominent Catholic family with his father, Ngô Đình Khả, being a high-ranking mandarin for Emperor Thành Thái during the French colonial era.
Succeeding his kinsman as ruler of Novgorod, this Varangian prince extended control along the Dnieper to Kiev and led a successful raid on Constantinople before his death in 912 — who was he?
Oleg the Wise: Varangian prince, founder of Kievan Rus'
The eldest daughter of a former president, she became the first woman elected head of state in South Korea — and in all of East Asia — before being removed from office in 2017. Who is she?

Park Geun-hye: President of South Korea from 2013 to 2017. Park previously served as the acting first lady of South Korea under her father's presidency from 1974 until her father's assassination in 1979.

Its name comes from Ancient Greek for "love of wisdom," and once upon a time physics and psychology were considered branches of it before going their separate academic ways. What rational, critical field is this?
Philosophy: Study of general and fundamental questions.

Nicknamed 'the Flautist' for his love of playing the flute at Dionysian festivals, this Macedonian-Greek king ruled Egypt twice and was a descendant of one of Alexander the Great's generals — who was he?
Ptolemy XII Auletes: Ptolemaic King of Egypt, 80–51 BC.

Turkish politician who rose from Istanbul mayor to prime minister (2003–2014) and has been president since 2014, co-founding the AKP. His rule has drawn criticism for democratic backsliding. Who is he?
Recep Tayyip Erdoğan: President of Turkey since 2014. Recep Tayyip Erdoğan (born 26 February 1954) is a Turkish politician and statesman who has been the president of Turkey since 2014.
The first person to walk to both the North and South Poles, this explorer later led his son on a 600-mile renewable-energy-only trek to the South Pole in 2017 — who is he?
The oldest daughter of her husband's own uncle, this woman was the wife of former Iraqi president Saddam Hussein and mother to sons Uday and Qusay — who is she?
Sajida Talfah: First wife of Saddam Hussein.
This 44-day conflict in 2020 ended in an Azerbaijani victory over Armenia and the breakaway state of Artsakh, with the defeat sparking anti-government protests in Yerevan — what was it?
Second Nagorno-Karabakh War: Conflict between Armenia and Azerbaijan (2020)
The first Iranian ever to win the Nobel Peace Prize, this lawyer and former judge was honored in 2003 for her work on democracy and women's, children's and refugee rights — who is she?

South by Southwest: American annual film and music festival.

Trajan: Roman emperor from AD 98 to 117.
This Roman goddess of love and beauty was claimed as an ancestor by Julius Caesar through her son Aeneas, survivor of the fall of Troy?
Venus (mythology): Ancient Roman goddess of love, sex and fertility.

William Wilberforce: English politician and abolitionist (1759–1833)
Once called 'perhaps the most famous singer alive' in much of Africa, this Senegalese star helped develop the mbalax genre and even served as his country's Minister of Tourism — who is he?

Stephanie Kwolek is a chemist. Stephanie Louise Kwolek (July 31, 1923 – June 18, 2014) was a Polish-American chemist known for inventing Kevlar (poly-paraphenylene terephthalamide).
What is the atomic number of Tennessine?
Tennessine is a synthetic element; it has symbol Ts and atomic number 117.
What is the atomic number of Astatine?
Astatine is a chemical element; it has symbol At and atomic number 85.
In what year did Tomitaro Makino die?
Tomitaro Makino (牧野 富太郎, Makino Tomitarō; 24 April 1862 – 18 January 1957) was a pioneer Japanese botanist noted for his taxonomic work.
In what year was Aluminium discovered?
Aluminium (the Commonwealth and preferred IUPAC name) or aluminum (North American English) is a chemical element; it has symbol Al and atomic number 13.
Which company manufactures Lockheed SR-71 Blackbird?
Lockheed SR-71 Blackbird: Skunk Works. The SR-71 was developed in the 1960s as a black project by Lockheed's Skunk Works division.
Cro-Magnon: France. Cro-Magnons produced Upper Palaeolithic cultures, the first major one being the Aurignacian, which was succeeded by the Gravettian by 30,000 years ago.
Who is credited with discovering Tucana?
Tucana: Petrus Plancius. Tucana (The Toucan) is a constellation in the southern sky, named after the toucan, a South American bird.
Who is credited with discovering Cro-Magnon?
Cro-Magnon: Louis Lartet. Cro-Magnons produced Upper Palaeolithic cultures, the first major one being the Aurignacian, which was succeeded by the Gravettian by 30,000 years ago.
Who is credited with discovering Makemake?
Makemake: Michael E. Brown. Makemake (minor-planet number 136472) is a dwarf planet orbiting the Sun in the Kuiper belt, a disc of icy bodies beyond the orbit of Neptune.
Found on every continent except Antarctica, this family of hook-billed raptors includes buzzards, vultures, and kites across 75 genera — which family is this?
Accipitridae is one of the four families within the order Accipitriformes, and is a family of small to large birds of prey with strongly hooked bills and variable morphology based on diet.
A close relative of the peach in the genus Prunus, this drupe's seed isn't a true nut and can be "blanched" by softening its skin in hot water before peeling — what is it?
This British-American theoretical physicist at the University of Illinois reshaped our understanding of superfluid helium, work crowned by the 2003 Nobel Prize in Physics — who was he?
Anthony Leggett (26 March 1938 - 8 March 2026) was a British-American theoretical physicist and professor at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (UIUC).
This common long-term inflammatory airway disease causes wheezing, coughing, and shortness of breath that can flare into sudden attacks triggered by allergens or pollen. What condition is it?
Asthma is a common long-term inflammatory disease of the airways. It is characterized by variable and recurring symptoms and reduced lung function.
Strawberries, blackcurrants and blueberries all count in the kitchen sense — though botanists would object, since the culinary meaning of this word differs from the scientific one. What word?
Berry is a small, pulpy, and often edible fruit.

Developed in Germany from the Old English Bulldog and the now-extinct Bullenbeisser, this medium-to-large mastiff-type dog breed is known for its square muzzle, underbite, and powerful bite — name the breed?
Boxer (dog breed) is a medium to large, short-haired dog breed of mastiff-type, developed in Germany.
The leaves and buds of this evergreen shrub, when processed differently, yield green, black, oolong, white, and yellow varieties of the world's most popular hot beverage — what's the species?
Camellia sinensis is a species of evergreen shrub or small tree in the flowering plant family Theaceae.
In calculus, this formula lets you find the derivative of a composed function h(x) = z(y(x)) using the derivatives of z and y separately — what is it called?
Chain rule is a formula that expresses the derivative of the composition of two differentiable functions z and y in terms of the derivatives of z and y.
Living in a symbiotic partnership with sea anemones that shelter them from predators, these Indo-Pacific reef fish live in groups led by a dominant breeding female. What fish are they?
Clownfish (genus Amphiprion) are saltwater fish found in the warm and tropical waters of the Indo-Pacific.
Which genus of passerine birds, whose Latin name literally means 'raven,' includes about 46 species commonly known as crows, ravens, and rooks?
Corvus is a widely distributed genus of passerine birds ranging from medium-sized to large-sized in the family Corvidae.
Used to treat ADHD and narcolepsy, this 'right-handed' mirror-image form of a stimulant molecule is also misused to boost cognitive and athletic performance — what is it?
Dextroamphetamine is a central nervous system (CNS) stimulant and enantiomer of amphetamine that is used in the treatment of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and narcolepsy.
Long used in traditional Indigenous medicine, this prairie-dwelling genus of purple daisy relatives gets its name from a Greek word meaning 'hedgehog' — what plant is it?
Echinacea is a genus of herbaceous flowering plants in the daisy family.

Discovered in January 2005 by a Palomar Observatory team and named after a Greco-Roman goddess of strife, this trans-Neptunian object is the most massive known dwarf planet in the solar system — which one?
Eris (dwarf planet) (minor-planet number 136199) is the most massive and second-largest known dwarf planet in the Solar System.
With over two hundred species across fifty genera, this bird family includes canaries, siskins, redpolls, grosbeaks, and the Hawaiian honeycreepers — which family of seed-eating passerines?
Finch are small to medium-sized passerine birds in the family Fringillidae.
Caused by abnormalities in the genome, this category of health problem may arise from a single faulty gene, many genes, or a chromosome abnormality — what is the general term?
Genetic disorder is a health problem caused by one or more abnormalities in the genome.
Nicknamed the 'benevolent dictator for life' of the language he invented, this Dutch programmer relinquished that title in July 2018. Who is he?
Guido van Rossum (born 31 January 1956) is a Dutch programmer.
This genus of the mallow family includes several hundred species prized for their large, showy blooms, and is sometimes known by the alternate name rose mallow — name the genus?
Hibiscus is a genus of common flowering plants in the mallow family, Malvaceae.
Prized in folk medicine as an antiseptic and expectorant, this Lamiaceae shrub grows wild from Southern Europe to the Caspian Sea area — which plant is it?
Hyssopus officinalis is a shrub in the Lamiaceae or mint family native to Southern Europe, the Middle East, and the region surrounding the Caspian Sea.
This Canadian-American physical educator invented an entire sport, wrote its original rule book after moving to the United States, and founded the University of Kansas's program in 1898 — who is he?
James Naismith (November 6, 1861 - November 28, 1939) was a Canadian-American physical educator, physician, Christian chaplain, and sports coach, best known as the inventor of the game of basketball.
Cousin to the wallaby and wallaroo in the family Macropodidae, this Australian marsupial's biggest member is the red one. What is it?
Kangaroo are marsupials from the subfamily Macropodinae (macropods, meaning "large foot").

Which citrus-scented perennial herb in the mint family, whose genus name Melissa comes from the Greek for 'honey bee,' is naturalized worldwide after originating in the Mediterranean and Central Asia?
Lemon balm (Melissa officinalis) is a perennial herbaceous plant in the mint family.
This Berkeley professor upended classical logic by proposing 'fuzzy' mathematics — fuzzy sets, fuzzy logic, fuzzy control, and more — who was he?

Lotfi A. Zadeh (4 February 1921 - 6 September 2017) was a mathematician, computer scientist, electrical engineer, artificial intelligence researcher, and professor of computer science at the University of California, Berkeley.
Sharing the 1963 Nobel Prize in Physics for work on nuclear shell structure, this German-American theorist became only the second woman ever to win that prize, after Marie Curie — who was she?
Maria Goeppert Mayer (ne Goppert; June 28, 1906 - February 20, 1972) was a German-American theoretical physicist who shared the 1963 Nobel Prize in Physics with J. Hans D. Jensen.
This branch of economics studies how individuals and firms allocate scarce resources within individual markets, as opposed to the economy as a whole — what field is it?

Microeconomics is a branch of economics that studies the behavior of individuals and firms in making decisions regarding the allocation of scarce resources and the interactions among these individuals and firms.
This semiaquatic rodent can stay submerged for up to seventeen minutes, propelled mainly by its webbed hind feet while its long, scaly tail helps steer — what animal is it?
Muskrat (Ondatra zibethicus) is a medium-sized semiaquatic rodent.
A reddish-brown gas that's a key step in making nitric acid for fertilizer, it also seeps into homes from gas-stove cooking and harms indoor air — which compound, formula NO2?
Nitrogen dioxide is a chemical compound with the formula NO2.

This group of middle-ear inflammations includes a painful acute infection that makes young children tug at their ears, plus a quieter form defined by non-infectious fluid lingering for weeks. What is the condition?
Otitis media is a group of inflammatory diseases of the middle ear.
Built for the sea, it sports a spiny tongue and powerful jaws to grip slippery fish, then swallows them whole mid-swim. Which animal splits its life half on land, half in the water?
Penguin are a group of flightless semi-aquatic sea birds which live almost exclusively in the Southern Hemisphere.
Native to South America and the most economically important member of the Bromeliaceae family, this tropical 'multiple fruit' became a 17th-century European symbol of luxury — what is it?
Pineapple (Ananas comosus) is a tropical plant with an edible fruit; it is the most economically significant plant in the family Bromeliaceae.

This male sexual dysfunction occurs when orgasm happens very soon after minimal sexual stimulation, with medical experts generally setting the threshold at around one minute — what's this condition called?

Premature ejaculation (PE) is a male sexual dysfunction that occurs when a male expels semen (and most likely experiences orgasm) soon after beginning sexual activity, and with minimal penile stimulation.
This colorless, odorless radioactive noble gas has the atomic number 86, and its longest-lived isotope has a half-life of under four days — name the element?
Radon is a chemical element; it has symbol Rn and atomic number 86.
Known by the common name 'dog rose,' this climbing wild rose species is native across Europe and stretches into northwest Africa and western Asia — which species?
Rosa canina is a variable climbing, wild rose species native to Europe, northwest Africa, and western Asia.

Seven living species make up this group of ocean-dwelling reptiles, five of which are threatened with extinction — one species, found only near Australia, Papua New Guinea, and Indonesia, is not — name this group?
Sea turtle (superfamily Chelonioidea), sometimes called marine turtles, are reptiles of the order Testudines and of the suborder Cryptodira.
Whether on land, in fresh water, or in the sea, this gastropod earns its name from a coiled shell roomy enough to fully retract into — what is it?
Snail is a shelled gastropod. The name is most often applied to land snails, terrestrial pulmonate gastropod molluscs.
This group of cartilaginous fish spans eleven families and roughly 220 species, from tiny river-dwellers to giant manta and devil rays — what group of fish is it?
Stingray are a group of rays, a type of cartilaginous fish.
This fibrous connective tissue connects muscle to bone, unlike its cousin which connects bone to bone, and numbers about 4,000 throughout the adult human body — what is it?
Tendon is a tough band of dense fibrous connective tissue that connects muscle to bone.
Caused by superantigens from staph or strep bacteria, this condition brings fever, a sunburn-like rash, and peeling skin, and has been tied to absorbent tampon use — which condition?
Toxic shock syndrome (TSS) is a condition caused by bacterial toxins.
This abnormal enlargement of the vein network draining the testicles is the most common correctable cause of male infertility, found in over a third of men with the condition. Name it?
Varicocele is an abnormal enlargement of the pampiniform venous plexus in the scrotum.
This biological process unfolds in predictable phases — hemostasis, inflammation, cell proliferation, and tissue remodeling — to replace damaged skin after the barrier is broken. What is it?
Wound healing refers to a living organism's replacement of destroyed or damaged tissue by newly produced tissue.
Unearthed in Montana by Jack Horner's team in 1987, this 20-foot horned dinosaur sported a bony neck-frill and lived roughly 75 million years ago — which species?
Achelousaurus: Genus of ceratopsid dinosaur from North America.
Often called the father of theoretical computer science, this Englishman gave us a famous 'machine' that formalized the very idea of computation — who was he?
Nicknamed 'whip-spiders' or 'tailless whip-scorpions,' these arachnids have no silk, no venom, and a name meaning 'blunt tail' — they grab with their pedipalps instead of biting — what order is this?
Amblypygi: Order of arachnids. The name "amblypygid" means "blunt tail", a reference to a lack of the flagellum that is otherwise seen in whip-scorpions.

Named from Greek words meaning "unlike other shrimp," this extinct arthropod from the Burgess Shale had swimming flaps, big compound eyes and grasping frontal appendages, reaching over a foot long — which prehistoric predator?
Anomalocaris: Extinct genus of cambrian radiodont.

Nicknamed for its resemblance to a stinging insect, this orb-weaver spider sports bold yellow, white, and black bands across Central and Northern Europe, parts of Asia and Africa, and even the Azores — what species is it?
Argiope bruennichi: Species of orb-weaver spider. Like many other members of the same genus Argiope, this species has distinctive yellow, white and black markings on its abdomen.
Native to tropical Southeast Asia, this small tree bears bell-shaped rose-to-purple flowers and a ridged fruit that forms star-shaped slices when cut crosswise — which species?
Averrhoa carambola: Species of tree. It is a small tree or shrub that grows 5 to 12 m (16 to 39 ft) tall, with rose to red-purple flowers.

When no one else had the staff for it, this American lawyer volunteered to prosecute the Einsatzgruppen trial at Nuremberg, then spent decades championing an International Criminal Court — who was he?

In this distributed ledger, each record holds a cryptographic hash of the one before it, so altering a single block would require rewriting every block that follows — making the data nearly tamper-proof. What is it?
Blockchain: Distributed data store for digital transactions.
This plant family — nicknamed the mustards or crucifers, and including cabbage — hosts the caterpillars of a notorious garden-pest butterfly as one of its worst enemies — name the family?
Native to tropical Africa, this gourd-producing vine yields fruit that can be eaten young as a vegetable or dried and hollowed out into bowls, ladles, or even musical instruments — what is it?
Calabash: Species of bottle gourd plant.
Ranked the world's richest person by Forbes from 2010 to 2013, this Mexican tycoon built his fortune largely through telecommunications and remains Latin America's wealthiest individual — who is he?
Around 20 millimetres long with a shimmering structural-green shell and a coppery underside, this beetle is identified by its isosceles-triangle scutellum — which species?
Cetonia aurata: Species of beetle. The scutellum is the small V-shaped area between the wing cases; it may show several small, irregular, white lines and marks.
Native to the Andean forests of South America, this genus of trees is nicknamed the 'fever tree' because its bark yields quinine, the only effective malaria treatment for centuries — what is it?
Cinchona: Genus of plants, source of quinine.
Making up a quarter to a third of all protein in mammals, this triple-helix fibrous protein needs vitamin C for its synthesis and gives structure to cartilage, tendons, and skin — what is it?
Collagen: Most abundant structural protein in animals.
First appearing in English in 1656 and later formalized in Latin by philosopher Christian Wolff, this field of study addresses the nature and origin of the universe — what field is it?
Cosmology: Study of the universe. Cosmology (from Ancient Greek κόσμος (cosmos) 'the universe, the world' and -λογία (logia) 'study of') is the study of the nature of the universe, the cosmos.
This biological process lets a cell make an exact copy of its genetic material by using each strand of the double helix as a template for a new one — what is it called?
DNA replication: Biological process. DNA replication ensures that each of the newly divided daughter cells receives its own copy of each DNA molecule.
Sold as Voltaren and taken by mouth, suppository, injection, skin gel, or even eye drops, this NSAID eases pain and inflammation like gout for up to eight hours a dose — what is it?
One of the very first vertebrate apex predators on Earth, this armor-plated, jointed-neck fish patrolled open Devonian seas some 380 million years ago — which genus?
This German chess player, mathematician and philosopher held the world title for 27 years — the longest reign ever — partly by a famously "psychological" approach to rattling opponents; who was he?

This branch of zoology studying animal behavior traces its scientific roots to Darwin and came into its own in the 1930s through Nobel laureates Tinbergen, Lorenz, and von Frisch — what's the field called?
Sold under the brand name Pepcid, this H2-receptor-blocking medication treats stomach-acid conditions like peptic ulcers and begins working within an hour — which drug?
Famotidine: Medication that reduces stomach acid.
Originally focused on water, this branch of physics studies liquids, gases, and plasmas, with applications from geophysics to aerospace engineering — which field?
Fluid mechanics: Branch of physics. Fluid mechanics is the branch of physics concerned with the mechanics of fluids (liquids, gases, and plasmas) and the forces on them.
Born in ancient Pergamon to a wealthy architect, this Roman-era Greek physician's writings shaped anatomy, physiology, and pharmacology for centuries — who was he?
Galen: Greek physician, surgeon, and philosopher (c. 129–216 AD)
Despite centuries of use in Korean and Chinese traditional medicine, no clinical evidence supports health claims for this Panax-genus root, often sold as a dietary supplement — what is it?
Ginseng: Root of a plant used in herbal preparations.

This algebraic structure — a set paired with an operation that's associative, has an identity element, and gives every member an inverse — is exemplified by the integers under addition. What is it called?

Group (mathematics): Set with associative invertible operation. The concept of a group was elaborated for handling, in a unified way, many mathematical structures such as numbers, geometric shapes and polynomial roots.
Nicknamed bindwood or lovestone, this clinging evergreen native to Europe scales tree trunks, walls, and fences — which plant?
Hedera helix: Species of flowering plant.

Widely credited as the 'father of the Indian nuclear programme,' this theoretical physicist founded the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research and chaired India's first Atomic Energy Commission — who is it?
Homi J. Bhabha: Indian nuclear physicist (1909–1966)
It usually causes no symptoms at all, yet this persistently elevated arterial pressure is a leading cause of stroke, heart failure and premature death worldwide — what's the medical name for it?
Hypertension: Long-term high blood pressure in the arteries.

Marked by an IQ below 70 and deficits in everyday adaptive skills first apparent in childhood, this neurodevelopmental condition was formerly called 'mental retardation' in the U.S. — what is it now called?
A French soldier turned naturalist, this early proponent of biological evolution published the three-volume 'Flore françoise' and joined the French Academy of Sciences in 1779 — who is he?
Nicknamed 'Iron Annie,' which corrugated-skin transport plane began life as a 1930 civilian airliner before Nazi Germany converted it for military use?
Situated between two larger folds of skin, these paired flaps extend from the inner vaginal and urethral openings and form the clitoral hood above — which structures are these?
Labia minora: Flaps of skin on either side of the vaginal opening in the vulva.
Cell signaling, homeostasis, metabolism, growth and reproduction are its hallmarks — and every instance of it eventually reaches death. What capacity in matter is this?

This Canadian physicist worked on the Manhattan Project determining critical mass values for uranium and plutonium, and in 1946 was fatally exposed to radiation in a lab accident at Los Alamos — who is he?
Louis Slotin: Canadian physicist and chemist (1910–1946)
Nicknamed sea cows, these slow-moving herbivorous mammals graze on more than 60 kinds of aquatic plants in the Caribbean, the Amazon basin, and West Africa — what are they?
Manatee: Genus of mammals. The main causes of death for manatees are human-related issues, such as habitat destruction and human objects.
This cone-shaped part of the brainstem controls involuntary functions from sneezing to heart rate, and was once known simply as 'the bulb' — which structure?
Medulla oblongata: Structure of the brain stem.
This branch of economics studies how individual firms and consumers allocate scarce resources, as opposed to the economy-wide view of its counterpart — which field?
Microeconomics: Behavior of individuals and firms.
The platypus and the four species of echidna are the only living mammals in this order that lay eggs rather than bear live young — what is it called?

Dropped from a B-52 and boosted by a modified Pegasus rocket stage before its own scramjet took over, this experimental hypersonic craft still holds the record for fastest jet-powered flight at about Mach 9.6 — what is it?
NASA X-43: Unmanned US experimental hypersonic aircraft, 1991-2000.

Named for a mythological daughter of Tantalus, this silvery transition metal with atomic number 41 was once called columbium and is now prized as a nickel-free option in hypoallergenic jewelry — which element?
Niobium: Chemical element with atomic number 41 (Nb)
Born in Nishapur during the Seljuk era, this Persian polymath solved general cubic equations using intersecting conic sections centuries before Descartes — who was he?
Omar Khayyam: Persian polymath and poet (1048–1131)
A perennial herb from the mountains of East Asia, its root is the original source of a famous herbal supplement — though studies find little evidence it actually works. Which plant?
Panax ginseng: Species of flowering plant.
Almost every member of this flightless, countershaded clan sticks to the Southern Hemisphere — except one lone species that creeps up to the equator in the Galapagos. What bird is it?
Penguin: Family of aquatic flightless birds.
Known across South Asia as Indian gooseberry or amla, this deciduous tree is native to tropical regions of the continent — which plant?
Phyllanthus emblica: Berry and plant. Phyllanthus emblica, commonly known as emblic, Indian gooseberry, amalaki, amloki, or amla, is a deciduous tree of the family Phyllanthaceae.

The most common hormonal disorder in women of reproductive age, it's diagnosed by two of three signs — irregular periods, high testosterone, or many antral follicles — despite a name that misleadingly implies true cysts. What's its newer name?
Polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome: Hormonal disorder in women. The exact cause of PMOS remains uncertain.
This Old World tree species has two main cultivar groups, the dark-red Morello and the lighter Amarelle, prized for their tart, edible pulp — which fruit-bearing plant?
Prunus cerasus: Species of cherry tree. Prunus cerasus (sour cherry, tart cherry, or dwarf cherry) is an Old World species of Prunus in the subgenus Cerasus (cherries).
A small herbivore of the family Leporidae and a cousin to hares, this prey animal has been introduced to every continent except Antarctica — what is it?
Rabbit: Mammals of the family Leporidae. The most widespread rabbit genera are Oryctolagus and Sylvilagus.
Responsible for at least half of all common colds, this tiny RNA virus in the Picornaviridae family measures only about 30 nanometers across — what is it?
A synthetic element named for a famous physicist, it's the first of the super-heavy transactinides and behaves chemically as the heavier cousin of hafnium in group 4 — which element?
Rutherfordium: Chemical element with atomic number 104 (Rf)
A predatory arachnid with eight legs, grasping pincers and a stinger-tipped tail, this desert-loving hunter has a lineage going back some 430 million years to the Silurian — what is it?
This crustacean typically swims forward using its swimmerets but can flick its tail to dart backward in a defensive move called 'lobstering' — what is it?
Also known as milo, jowar, or Guinea corn, this grass — domesticated in Sudan and now grown worldwide — ranks as the fifth most important cereal crop on Earth — which grain?
Sorghum: Species of grain. It is typically an annual, but some cultivars are perennial.

These long-legged wading birds communicate by clattering their bills rather than calling, favor drier habitats than their heron cousins, and are collectively known as a 'muster' or a 'phalanx' — which birds?
Commonly known as the pork tapeworm, this parasite completes its life cycle by cycling between human waste, pig feed, and undercooked pork — which species?
Taenia solium: Species of tapeworm. Taenia solium, the pork tapeworm, belongs to the cyclophyllid cestode family Taeniidae.

Taught in universities and seminaries, this academic discipline studies religious belief from within a religious perspective, focusing on divinity, revelation, and how God might interact with the world — what field is it?
Theology: Study of the nature of deities and religious beliefs.
This field of geoscience studies the shape of land surfaces — not just elevation, but roads, boundaries, and buildings too, as shown on USGS terrain maps — what is it called?
Topography: Study of the forms of land surfaces in earth.

This late Cretaceous carnivore, whose scientific name pairs a word for 'tyrant' with the Latin for 'king,' roamed western North America right up until the mass extinction 66 million years ago — which iconic predator is it?
Tyrannosaurus: Genus of Late Cretaceous theropod.
Native to southwestern Europe, this venomous viper is also called the asp or aspic viper, with about 4% of untreated bites proving fatal — which snake?
Vipera aspis: Species of snake. Its common names include asp, asp viper, European asp, and aspic viper, among others.
Aboard Apollo 8, the first crewed mission to leave low Earth orbit, this astronaut snapped the iconic "Earthrise" photograph as the crew circled the Moon ten times — who took it?
William Anders: American astronaut and lunar explorer (1933–2024)

The symbol for lanthanum is La. Lanthanum is a chemical element; it has symbol La and atomic number 57.

Heath Ledger: Heath Andrew Ledger (4 April 1979 – 22 January 2008) was an Australian actor.

In what year was The Name of the Rose first released?

12 Monkeys: It stars Bruce Willis, Madeleine Stowe, Brad Pitt, and Christopher Plummer.

Batman Returns is a 1992 American superhero film directed by Tim Burton and written by Daniel Waters.
